main_text.p: Eædem literæ Gjim, Hha, & Cha, cùm literæ præcedenti conjunguntur, illum supra lineam plerunque (non semper) attollunt, ut in [illegible, ~8 letters] &c.

Kef sæpè in principio sic [illegible, ~1 letter], & in medio sic [illegible, ~1 letter] pingitur. Varie vero sibi invicem connectuntur literæ apud Arabes, qui καλλιγραφίας studiosissimi sunt: præcipuas ligaturarum hic annectemus.

page.notes: The Arabic letter forms and ligatures are printed as images. Their individual glyphs could not be read reliably, so they are marked illegible; the Latin words, the Greek word καλλιγραφίας and the names of the letters are transcribed as printed. The first ligature line and the "&c." line may have further glyphs not fully legible. The final glyph at the lower right stands alone and is treated as its own line. The reference to "Gain" and "Ain" appears as printed.
